Details: Send personalized review request email 30 days after membership start. Include direct Google review link. See assets/review-request-templates.md.
Why It Matters: First 25 reviews are the difference between invisible and credible. 30 days = enough time to have experienced value.

Details: After a resolved care episode, clinician sends: "Glad we could help. If you have a moment, a Google review helps other patients find care like this." + link.
Why It Matters: Contextual ask after a positive moment has highest conversion. Clinician trust = highest response rate.

Details: 24 hours after welcome call, send: "Thanks for taking the time today. If you're comfortable, a quick review helps others discover Present Health." + link.
Why It Matters: Welcome call is a high-trust moment. First impression is usually positive. Capture that sentiment immediately.

Details: Generate a short URL for Google review (from GBP dashboard). Use this single link everywhere.
Why It Matters: Friction kills reviews. A direct link that opens the review form (not just the listing) doubles completion rate.

Details: Respond to EVERY review within 24 hours. Use HIPAA-safe templates (see assets/review-response-templates.md). Never acknowledge medical details.
Why It Matters: Response rate signals active management to Google. Responded-to reviews signal trust to prospective patients. HIPAA violations in responses = legal risk.

Details: Track: total reviews, average rating, response time, review velocity. Dashboard already exists in admin.
Why It Matters: Trend tracking reveals whether strategy is working. Review velocity (reviews/month) is the metric that matters for ranking.

Details: Ensure physician profiles on Healthgrades, Zocdoc, and Vitals are claimed and match GBP NAP. These feed Google's trust signals.
Why It Matters: Directory profiles are citation sources. Consistent NAP (name, address, phone) across directories is a core local ranking factor.

Details: List on: DPC Alliance (dpcare.org), DPC Frontier Mapper (mapper.dpcfrontier.com), FindMyDirectDoctor.com, DPCPractices.com. Include pricing, states, and description.
Why It Matters: DPC directories rank for "DPC near me" and "direct primary care [state]." Being listed captures referral traffic from patients actively searching for DPC.

Details: Do NOT filter or gate reviews (e.g., asking happy patients to review publicly and unhappy patients to email privately). Google prohibits this and will penalize the listing.
Why It Matters: Review gating violates Google's policies and FTC guidelines. If caught, listing can be suspended. All patients get the same ask.

Details: Month 1: 5 reviews. Month 2: 12 reviews. Month 3: 25 reviews. Month 6: 50 reviews. Maintain 4.5+ average.
Why It Matters: 5 reviews = star rating appears. 25 reviews = competitive with local DPCs. 50 reviews = trust parity with established practices.
